articles.title: What Prefill Was and Why It Disappeared

blocks.content: Prefill consisted of placing a message with role: "assistant" at the end of messages, as if Claude had already started responding. The model would continue exactly from there, instead of generating a response from scratch.

blocks.title: Removed in current models
blocks.content: Prefill isn't supported in claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-4-8, or claude-haiku-4-5-20251001. Requests that use it return a 400 error. Anthropic removed it because it was a generation trick, not a real guarantee: it didn't ensure valid JSON, consumed context tokens with no clear attribution, and conflicts with extended thinking, where the model needs to control its own response flow.

subsections.title: The same trick existed in AWS Bedrock

blocks.content: Bedrock's Converse API supported exactly the same mechanism: adding a message with `role: "assistant"` at the end of `messages` so Claude would continue from there instead of generating from scratch (see Claude API → Claude on AWS Bedrock → Multi-turn conversations for the `add_user_message` / `add_assistant_message` helpers).

blocks.code:
messages = []
add_user_message(messages, "Is coffee or tea better for breakfast?")
add_assistant_message(messages, "Coffee is better because")

chat(messages)
# used to return the continuation, e.g. "it has more caffeine."
# you had to concatenate the prefill + the continuation to get the full response

blocks.title: It wasn't a Bedrock feature, it was model behavior
blocks.content: Prefill was never a capability of the direct API or of Bedrock's Converse API itself — it depended on how the underlying model interpreted an assistant message at the end of the conversation. That's why its removal in current models (Claude 4.6 onward) has no documented per-platform exception: it applies the same regardless of whether you invoke the model via api.anthropic.com or via Bedrock. The modern alternatives carry over directly too: strict tool use via `toolConfig`, and moving tone or persona instructions into the Converse API's `system`.
Prefill was mostly used for three situations. Each has a direct, more robust replacement in current models.

rows.value: Prefilling "The answer is (" and requesting 1 token.
Prefilling "{" so Claude starts directly with JSON.
Prefilling "[Detective Morgan]" at the start of every turn.
Strict tool use with enum: guarantees one of the exact values, no text parsing needed.
output_config.format with json_schema: a real API-level guarantee, not probabilistic.
Instruction in the system prompt: applies to the whole conversation without fake messages.

subsections.title: Case 1: Multiple choice → Strict tool use

blocks.content: Instead of prefilling "The answer is (", you define a tool with strict: true and an enum with the valid options. Claude is required to call the tool with one of those exact values — there's no text to parse.

blocks.title: strict: true vs. without strict
blocks.content: With strict: true and additionalProperties: False, Claude is required to produce exactly the schema's fields, with no extras or variations. Without strict, the schema is a strong guide but not an absolute guarantee.

subsections.title: Case 2: JSON with a specific shape → output_config.format

blocks.content: Previously, "{" was prefilled to force Claude to skip the preamble and start directly with JSON. Now output_config.format guarantees the full structure at the API level, without relying on a generation trick.

blocks.title: output_config.format is incompatible with prefill
blocks.content: There's no need to combine it with prefill: it already solves the same problem in a guaranteed way instead of a probabilistic one.

There's an equivalent alternative, older than output_config.format and still widely used: forcing tool_choice on a tool that doesn't represent a real action, but only the schema of the data to extract. Claude "calls" that tool with the JSON in its input field instead of generating it as text.

blocks.title: No second request: this isn't real tool use
blocks.content: Since the tool doesn't actually execute anything, the flow ends as soon as `input` is read — there's no need to assemble a `tool_result` or send it back to Claude. This sets it apart from the normal tool-use loop (see The multi-turn loop), where the `tool_result` is required to close the turn.

blocks.title: Forced tool or output_config.format?
blocks.content: Both give a real structural guarantee. output_config.format is more direct when the only goal is JSON (without the conceptual noise of a "tool" that does nothing) and is the newer option. Forcing a tool with tool_choice is still preferable if the schema needs `strict: true` with validation logic you already have set up for real tools, or in SDKs/integrations where tools is already the established mechanism for all structured output.

subsections.title: Extension of Case 2: prefill + stop_sequences to delimit any format

blocks.content: Beyond JSON, the same trick of prefilling an opening delimiter was combined with a stop sequence on the closing delimiter to capture Python code, CSV, lists, or config files without the explanatory text Claude adds around them by default.

blocks.code:
messages = []
add_user_message(messages, "Generate a very short EventBridge rule as JSON")
add_assistant_message(messages, "```json")

text = chat(messages, stop_sequences=["```"])
# Claude "believes" it already opened the code block and continues straight into the JSON;
# as soon as it tries to close with ``` again, the stop_sequence cuts it off there.
# text ends up with only the content, without the opening or closing ```.

blocks.title: The prefill half of this combo is deprecated — stop_sequences isn't
blocks.content: add_assistant_message(messages, "```json") is prefill: it inherits the same removal in Claude 4.6+ as the rest of this page (see above, and its Bedrock equivalent). stop_sequences still works exactly the same — what stopped working is the half that opened the delimiter.

The replacement depends on the format. For JSON, output_config.format (above) is still the most solid option. For formats without a formal schema — code, CSV, lists — the modern alternative is to directly ask Claude to wrap the content in its own XML tag and extract it with a string split; Claude respects a tag boundary much more consistently than a vague instruction like "don't add extra text" (see Claude API → Prompt Engineering → XML Tags).

blocks.code:
add_user_message(messages, "Generate a very short EventBridge rule as JSON. "
                            "Wrap it in <output> tags with nothing else inside them.")
response = chat(messages)

text = response.split("<output>")[1].split("</output>")[0].strip()

subsections.title: Case 3: Maintaining tone or persona → System prompt

blocks.content: When prefill was used to reinforce a role at the start of every turn, the replacement is to move that instruction into system, where it applies to the whole conversation without depending on a fake assistant message.

blocks.code:
response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-sonnet-4-6",
    max_tokens=1024,
    system="Always respond in character as Detective Morgan: dry tone, "
           "precise observations, no beating around the bush. Never break "
           "character or add explanations outside their voice.",
    messages=[
        {"role": "user", "content": "What did you find at the scene?"},
    ],
)
# Claude responds directly as Detective Morgan,
# with no preamble or breaking of character

blocks.title: The system prompt also works to skip the preamble
blocks.content: If the problem was that Claude started with "Sure, here you go...", the fix is adding to the system: "Respond directly, without introductory phrases." It's more reliable than prefill because it applies to the entire session.

Prefill never guaranteed anything: it only influenced the probability of the continuation. The three alternatives are more explicit and, for the schema cases, give a real guarantee instead of a probabilistic suggestion.

items.title: I want one of N exact options
items.body: Strict tool use with enum. Claude is required to return one of the listed values. Ideal for classifiers, multiple-choice answers, routing.

items.title: I want JSON with a specific shape
items.body: output_config.format with json_schema. A real API-level guarantee. Ideal for data extraction, internal APIs that consume Claude's output.

items.title: I want to control tone, style, or persona
items.body: System prompt. Applies to the whole conversation, no fake assistant messages, and can be cached with cache_control for long conversations.

items.title: I want to skip the preamble
items.body: System prompt with an explicit instruction: "Respond directly with no introduction." More reliable than prefill because it applies to the entire session.
